desc:
You are given an integer array nums (not sorted) and a list of queries. Each query is [left, right, value]; its answer is the number of indices i with left ≤ i ≤ right and nums[i] == value.

Return the answers to all queries as an array, in the order of the queries.
hints: Counting inside each range costs O(n) per query, which can be too slow for many queries. Think about the positions of one value.
For every distinct value, store the sorted list of indices where it occurs (build it with one left-to-right pass).
A query asks how many positions in that sorted list fall in [left, right]. That is upper_bound(right) - lower_bound(left) inside the list; an unseen value gives 0.
editorial: Group the indices by value: positions[v] is the list of indices holding v, which is already sorted because we append while scanning from left to right. For a query (l, r, v) the answer is the number of entries of positions[v] between l and r inclusive.

In a sorted list that count is the index of the first entry greater than r (upper bound) minus the index of the first entry at least l (lower bound). The preprocessing is O(n); every query costs O(log n), so the total is O(n + q log n). The same idea answers 'how many elements of a sorted array lie in [lo, hi]' with two bounds.
